internal.title: Incident Report: Elevated Error Rate and Latency in Checkout Service
internal.body:
At 11:54 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered for the checkout service due to a high error rate of 9.5% and elevated p95 latency of 400 ms. Initial diagnosis identified error injection within the checkout service as the primary issue, supported by metrics indicating increased errors. Resource exhaustion was considered but ruled out as CPU utilization was only at 25%, not indicative of resource constraints.

Multiple diagnosis rounds refined the understanding of the issue, with hypotheses focusing on error injection and latency within the checkout service. Attempts to mitigate by toggling flags were blocked due to mismatches in target conditions. The issue was escalated for further investigation and resolution.

No immediate resolution actions were successful during the incident window, and the root cause remains under investigation. The incident highlights the need for improved guardrail configurations to allow more flexible mitigation actions and enhanced monitoring to detect early signs of error injection.

Timeline highlights:
- 11:54 UTC: Alert received for high error rate
- 12:13 UTC: Diagnosis confirmed error injection and latency issues
- 12:14 UTC: Multiple replans and guardrail blocks on mitigation proposals

Further analysis and remediation steps are ongoing.

external.title: Checkout Service Experiencing Intermittent Errors and Delays
external.body: Between 11:54 and 12:14 UTC on 2026-11-08, some customers experienced difficulties completing their checkout process due to intermittent errors and slower response times. Our engineering team identified increased error rates and latency within the checkout service during this period. We are actively investigating the root cause and working to restore full service reliability. We apologize for any inconvenience caused and appreciate your patience.
